title: WEER by Natalie Palamides at the Cherry Lane Theatre #nataliepalamide...
transcript: Okay, this is one of my favorite theatre pieces I've seen all year and I'm surprised that not more people are talking about it because I think it's like a must-see. it's playing at the Cherry Lane Theatre in the West Village which was recently purchased by A24 and I think this is actually the first like theatrical production they're producing there since acquiring it. anyway, it's a comedy by Natalie Palamides, she's the writer and performer. and it's a ROM-com and she plays both characters. so it's like Christina and Mark, and essentially Mark is played by like the right half of her body and Christina is played by the left half of her body. so she plays both characters, and it's just her with some audience participation. the whole one side is one character, the other side is other character it's, it's a pretty elementary gag but like, she makes it go on for like 90 minutes, it's like really impressive. I think this is like an exercise in committing to the bit like to the extreme. I really don't wanna give away too much but it it's outrageous it's so, so funny. like the things that she comes up with, like how far she gets this to go is is really crazy. parts of it are really like vulgar and lowbrow and just chaotic, but it's really really well crafted and very smart. the comedy is so immediate and visceral, and like the whole thing is so chaotic in the best way possible. like I said, there's some audience participation, and there's some like fourth wall breaks that are like really funny um and just really well timed. but the audience participation is kind of not like what you would expect, it's there's some call and response, there's some like, other people that kind of come in as like characters like for a brief moments here, it's it's really funny but it's not too much. and even if you're not like integrated into the play itself if you're sitting like in the first row or two, you're in what they would consider a splash zone. and actually the front row is provided ponchos for this very reason, so there's a lot of crazy stuff happens. Natalie's performance in this is so impressive, like her comedy is so physical, it's so fearless and like balls to the walls just it's just really impressive. and I think her mind has to be doing so much code switching live, and she does some like improvisational moments like she's really really in the moment with the audience and it's the kind of experience that you can only have live, like this wouldn't translate in any other medium because of how um spontaneous a lot of it feels. while I was watching this, I was reminded of how I felt when I first saw Oh, Mary! starring Cole Escola. it's such a singular performance and creative mind at the helm of the project. everything works so perfectly but it's it's so out there that you just kind of feel like oh my gosh like only a geniusly unhinged person could have made this. I didn't know anything about Natalie Palamides before seeing her in this show, so I did like a brief search of her afterwards and it looks like her background is in comedy, and she has a comedy special that you can stream on Netflix if you wanna familiarize yourself with her at all. I don't know how similar that is to this show, but in any case I cannot recommend this enough. Weer at the Cherry Lane Theatre, I thought it was amazing. it's currently running until November 9th and it looks like it's fully sold out but I've been following the Cherry Lane's Instagram and on their stories like sometimes they announce like little ticket drops here and there, so just keep an eye out. and I know that they also do an in person rush. I hope more people get a chance to see this or that maybe they'll extend it or do some sort of encore run at some point. with that, another program for my collection
